burgess hill.s1_head: Charity and volunteer kit in Burgess Hill
s1loc: Burgess Hill sits in Mid Sussex, and its charity sector is busy. Burgess Hill Community Food Bank, going since 2013, sorts donations and hands out parcels from its premises with satellite points in Hassocks and Hurstpierpoint, all run by volunteers. The Burgess Hill and District Pantry offers a dignified shopping experience, while UKHarvest runs a monthly Community Food Hub at The King's Church. The big food-redistribution and foodbank networks back the work, so demand for affordable, hard-wearing workwear runs through the town all year.

The sector here runs at every size. National and regional charities keep shops with central buying and trade accounts, while small community groups, foodbanks, pantries and volunteer-run projects work on a shoestring across St Andrews, Victoria, Leylands and Franklands. We are glad to outfit the national charity ordering in bulk and the one-room foodbank alike, with proper trade accounts for the larger names and direct online ordering with no minimum for the smallest group, keeping every pound off the cause.

There is real depth beyond the food banks. St Peter and St James Hospice runs its charity shop on Church Road, one of nine across Mid Sussex raising funds for community palliative care, and Neighbourly Care fields DBS-checked volunteers for shopping, prescriptions and befriending calls. Community People supports volunteering across the town, and the UKHarvest food hub draws over thirty support agencies. Mutual-aid groups and warm spaces across Hassocks and Hurstpierpoint lean on washable, low-cost kit that puts donors' money where it matters most.
